info.title: heapscope-cli
info.description: HeapScope's command line: capture (Windows and Linux; macOS untested) and analyze .NET memory dumps and gcdumps, from heap summaries to retention paths and leak detectors.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --pipe
options.description: Attach to a worker already listening on this pipe instead of starting one.

options.name: --dac-folder
options.description: A folder holding mscordaccore.dll of the dumped runtime, when that runtime is not installed here.

options.name: --allow-symbol-server
options.description: Allow downloading a missing mscordaccore.dll from Microsoft's symbol server (sends module identifiers, never dump contents). [default: False]

options.name: --trust-dac
options.description: Trust the DAC next to a dump with this SHA-256 for this run (the refusal names it). Repeat for several.

commands.name: worker
commands.description: Commands for the analysis worker process.

commands.name: ping
commands.description: Start (or attach to) the analysis worker and measure a round trip.

commands.name: info
commands.description: Show the analysis worker's version, process and memory.

commands.name: synthetic
commands.description: Build a synthetic object graph in the worker (diagnostics). Ctrl+C cancels.

options.name: --objects
options.description: Number of objects. [default: 5000000]

options.name: --refs
options.description: Average references per object. [default: 3]

options.name: --seed
options.description: Random seed. [default: 42]

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of types to list. [default: 10]

commands.name: open
commands.description: Open a full dump: load it (or reuse its index cache) and print a summary. Ctrl+C cancels.

options.name: --rebuild
options.description: Ignore an existing index cache and load the dump again. [default: False]

options.name: --mode
options.description: Memory mode: auto, memory or mapped. [default: auto]

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of types to list. [default: 20]

options.name: --no-overcommit
options.description: Fail instead of warning when the load may not fit in available memory. [default: False]

arguments.name: DUMP
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp).

commands.name: summary
commands.description: Summarize a dump by type, namespace, assembly or interface (opens it first; reuses its index cache). Ctrl+C cancels.

options.name: --group
options.description: Rows per type, namespace, assembly or interface (full dumps; a type counts under each interface it implements). [default: type]

options.name: --filter
options.description: Keep rows whose name matches: lower case ignores case; capitals match as typed or as CamelHumps (SCE finds StaticCacheEntry); * matches anything.

options.name: --sort
options.description: Sort by bytes, count, name or retained (adds the retained column). [default: bytes]

options.name: --retained
options.description: Add retained bytes per row: a lower bound, the bytes its objects keep alive that no other object of the row holds (computes the snapshot's dominators the first time, then reuses them). [default: False]

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of rows. [default: 25]

options.name: --all
options.description: Print every row. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: DUMP
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp).

commands.name: diff
commands.description: Compare two dumps by type: objects and bytes in each and their growth (opens them first; reuses their index caches). Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 grew more than --fail-on-growth, 1 error, 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --group
options.description: Rows per type, namespace, assembly or interface (full dumps; a type counts under each interface it implements). [default: type]

options.name: --filter
options.description: Keep rows whose name matches: lower case ignores case; capitals match as typed or as CamelHumps (SCE finds StaticCacheEntry); * matches anything. --fail-on-growth checks only the matching rows.

options.name: --sort
options.description: Sort column, descending: bytes-delta, count-delta, bytes, count, baseline-bytes, baseline-count, name, new, dead, retained-delta, gen2-delta. [default: bytes-delta]

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of rows. [default: 25]

options.name: --all
options.description: Print every row. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

options.name: --fail-on-growth
options.description: Exit with code 2 when the matching rows grew by more than this: a size (50MB, 512KB, 1GB, or bytes) or a percent of their baseline bytes (10%; anything growing from zero bytes exceeds every percent). Dumps count unreachable objects not yet collected, so for a stable gate capture both after a full GC in the target (GC.Collect, GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers, GC.Collect). Not with --match-objects: a forced GC between the dumps moves most objects, so they match as dead and new.

options.name: --match-objects
options.description: Add New and Dead objects per row, matched by address and type: only for two dumps of one process (sprint 3.3). An object moved by a compacting GC counts as dead and new. [default: False]

options.name: --retained
options.description: Add each row's retained bytes in both dumps and the delta (lower bounds; computes each dump's dominators the first time). [default: False]

options.name: --growth-of
options.description: What --fail-on-growth checks: total bytes (default) or one heap kind's bytes (gen0, gen1, gen2, loh, poh; with a size, not a percent). [default: total]

options.name: --fail-on-growth-per-row
options.description: Check --fail-on-growth against each matching row on its own (a percent against that row's baseline bytes), so one growing type cannot hide behind a shrinking one. [default: False]

arguments.name: BASELINE
arguments.description: The earlier dump (.dmp); deltas are current minus baseline.

commands.name: trend
commands.description: Compare several dumps at once: each type's objects and bytes in every dump (oldest first), the change from the first to the last, and the steps it grew in. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --group
options.description: Rows per type, namespace, assembly or interface (full dumps; a type counts under each interface it implements). [default: type]

options.name: --filter
options.description: Keep rows whose name matches: lower case ignores case; capitals match as typed or as CamelHumps (SCE finds StaticCacheEntry); * matches anything.

options.name: --sort
options.description: Sort column, descending: bytes-delta, count-delta, growth-steps or name. [default: bytes-delta]

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of rows. [default: 25]

options.name: --all
options.description: Print every row. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: DUMPS
arguments.description: Two to twenty dumps, oldest first.

commands.name: instances
commands.description: List the objects of a type: address, size, generation, and a string's text or an array's length (opens the dump first; reuses its index cache). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --type
options.description: The type's full name, as the summary prints it (System.String, System.Byte[]).

options.name: --module
options.description: The type's module file name (System.Private.CoreLib.dll); needed only when types in several modules share the name.

options.name: --filter
options.description: Keep objects whose address starts with this (0x1f2a), whose value matches a regular expression (/^Get.*Async$/), or whose value contains this text (any case).

options.name: --sort
options.description: Sort by bytes, address, generation, value or retained (adds the retained column). [default: bytes]

options.name: --retained
options.description: Add each object's retained bytes: what it alone keeps alive (computes the snapshot's dominators the first time, then reuses them). [default: False]

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of rows. [default: 25]

options.name: --all
options.description: Print every row. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: DUMP
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp).

commands.name: object
commands.description: Show one object: type, size, generation, whether a root holds it, its fields (nested) and the objects it references (opens the dump first; reuses its index cache). A snapshot that cannot read fields (a gcdump) prints why on stderr. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error (such as no object at the address), 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --references
options.description: Outgoing references to print (0 for none). [default: 50]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: text or json. [default: text]

options.name: --retained
options.description: Add the object's retained bytes and its immediate dominator, the closest object every path from a root to it passes through (computes the snapshot's dominators the first time, then reuses them). [default: False]

arguments.name: DUMP
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp).

arguments.name: ADDRESS
arguments.description: The object's address in hex, as 'instances' prints it (0x1f2a3b40).

commands.name: referrers
commands.description: List who references an object (--address) or the objects of a type (--type, grouped by the referrers' type). The first query of a snapshot builds its incoming references index and saves it next to the index cache. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --address
options.description: The object's address in hex (0x1f2a3b40): list the objects referencing it.

options.name: --type
options.description: A type's full name (System.String): list the types whose objects reference its objects.

options.name: --module
options.description: With --type: the type's module file name; needed only when types in several modules share the name.

options.name: --sort
options.description: With --type: sort by references, objects, targets, bytes or type. [default: references]

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of rows. [default: 25]

options.name: --all
options.description: Print every row. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: SNAPSHOT
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp) or gcdump (.gcdump).

commands.name: paths
commands.description: Explain why an object (--address) or the objects of a type (--type) are alive: shortest paths from GC roots, roots in plain language, field names on full dumps. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error (no such object or type), 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --address
options.description: An object's address in hex (0x1f2a3b40): why is it alive?

options.name: --type
options.description: A type's full name: why are its objects alive (their key retention paths)?

options.name: --module
options.description: With --type: the type's module file name, when several modules have the name.

options.name: --max
options.description: Roots to find for --address (1 to 50, default 10), key paths to list for --type (1 to 100, default 20).

options.name: --expand
options.description: Show every framework step instead of folding runs of them. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: text or json. [default: text]

arguments.name: SNAPSHOT
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp) or gcdump (.gcdump).

commands.name: retainers
commands.description: Show the biggest retainers: the objects that alone keep the most memory alive, as the top of the dominator tree, expanded --depth levels (or the tree below --address). The first query of a snapshot computes its dominators and saves them next to the index cache. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --address
options.description: Show the tree below this object (hex, 0x1f2a3b40) instead of the biggest retainers.

options.name: --group
options.description: Children as objects (none) or grouped by type or namespace. [default: none]

options.name: --depth
options.description: Levels to expand below the top (0 to 5). [default: 0]

options.name: --top
options.description: Rows per level: the biggest children of each expanded row (1 to 1,000). [default: 20]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: SNAPSHOT
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp) or gcdump (.gcdump).

commands.name: retained-by
commands.description: Show what every object of a type keeps alive together, exactly, by type, next to the summary's per-type lower bound (which leaves out what several of them hold together). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error (no such type), 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --module
options.description: The type's module file name; needed only when types in several modules share the name.

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of rows. [default: 25]

options.name: --all
options.description: Print every row. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: SNAPSHOT
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp) or gcdump (.gcdump).

commands.name: set
commands.description: Show a set of objects, chosen by type, namespace, assembly, interface, address, inspection row or as the objects no root reaches, in one of the app's set views. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error (the set selects nothing), 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --type
options.description: A type's full name; repeat for several types.

options.name: --module
options.description: The types' module file name; needed only when types in several modules share a name.

options.name: --namespace
options.description: Every type of a namespace, as the summary's namespace rows name them.

options.name: --assembly
options.description: Every type of an assembly, by its module file name (Leaks.dll).

options.name: --interface
options.description: Every type implementing an interface, by its full name (full dumps).

options.name: --unreachable
options.description: The objects no root reaches: garbage the full dump still holds; objects waiting for their finalizer are not in it (sprint 3.5; full dumps with a complete graph). [default: False]

options.name: --address
options.description: An object's address (0x...); repeat for several objects.

options.name: --inspection
options.description: An inspection's name; with --row, the objects behind that row.

options.name: --row
options.description: The inspection row's number, from 0, in the order 'inspect' lists the rows. [default: -1]

options.name: --baseline
options.description: The earlier dump an inspection that compares against one uses.

options.name: --compared-with
options.description: Another dump of the same process: with --change, the set's new, dead or survived objects matched by address (sprint 3.3). Dead objects are in the earlier dump, so give the earlier dump as the snapshot and the later one here.

options.name: --change
options.description: new, dead or survived, with --compared-with.

options.name: --similar-group
options.description: One Similar Retention group of the chosen set, by its number (from 1) as the similar view lists them. [default: 0]

options.name: --retained
options.description: The objects the set keeps alive together instead of its own members. [default: False]

options.name: --view
options.description: types, instances, generations, dominators (the members no other member dominates), retained (what the set keeps alive, by type), paths (key retention paths) or similar (Similar Retention: members grouped by how they are retained, numbered from 1). [default: types]

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of rows. [default: 25]

options.name: --all
options.description: Print every row. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: SNAPSHOT
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp) or gcdump (.gcdump).

commands.name: inspect
commands.description: Find common memory waste (duplicate strings, empty and oversized collections, sparse and large arrays, the large object heap, finalizable objects, fragmentation) and name leaks (growing static collections, event handlers, timers, disposed but referenced objects, HttpClient instances, undisposed service scopes). Opens the dump first and reuses its index cache. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error (an unknown or unavailable inspection), 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --baseline
options.description: An earlier dump of the same process: the leak detectors that measure growth (growing-static-collections) compare with it (sprint 2.6).

options.name: --top
options.description: Number of rows. [default: 25]

options.name: --all
options.description: Print every row. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: DUMP
arguments.description: Path of the full memory dump (.dmp).

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The inspection: duplicate-strings, empty-collections, oversized-collections, sparse-arrays, large-arrays, loh, finalizable, fragmentation, or a leak detector: growing-static-collections, event-handler-leaks, timer-leaks, disposed-but-referenced, httpclient-instances, undisposed-service-scopes. Leave out to run all and print a summary.

commands.name: trace
commands.description: Record an EventPipe trace of a running .NET process (read it with PerfView or Visual Studio). Ctrl+C stops the recording and keeps it.

options.name: --pid
options.description: Process id to trace (see 'list').

options.name: --duration
options.description: Seconds to record (Ctrl+C stops earlier and keeps the trace). [default: 30]

options.name: --profile
options.description: cpu: CPU samples with call stacks. gc: collections, pauses and sampled allocations. allocations: sampled allocations with call stacks (read it with 'allocations'). [default: cpu]

options.name: --out
options.description: The .nettrace file to write; default: <process>-<pid>-<time>.nettrace in the current folder.

commands.name: allocations
commands.description: Show what allocated the most while an allocations trace recorded: the top types and the top call stacks of an interval. Sizes are estimates from samples (about one per 100 KB). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --from
options.description: Start of the interval, in seconds since the trace started. [default: 0]

options.name: --to
options.description: End of the interval, in seconds (default: the end of the trace).

options.name: --type
options.description: Only allocations of this type (its full name, as the types table prints it).

options.name: --types
options.description: Types to list (0 to 1,000). [default: 10]

options.name: --stacks
options.description: Call stacks to list (1 to 1,000). [default: 10]

options.name: --frames
options.description: Frames printed per stack in the table, the allocating method first (1 to 100). [default: 12]

options.name: --view
options.description: What to print: summary (types and stacks), types or stacks. CSV needs types or stacks. [default: summary]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table, csv or json. [default: table]

arguments.name: TRACE
arguments.description: Path of an allocations trace (.nettrace), from 'trace --profile allocations' or HeapScope's Record allocations.

commands.name: monitor
commands.description: Watch a process's GC heap, collections and allocations every interval, and capture full dumps (or gcdumps, --kind gcdump) into the current session when rules fire. Ctrl+C stops. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 64 usage, 130 canceled.

options.name: --pid
options.description: Process id to monitor (see 'list').

options.name: --interval
options.description: Seconds between samples. [default: 1]

options.name: --duration
options.description: Seconds to monitor; default: until Ctrl+C or the process exits.

options.name: --every
options.description: Take a snapshot every interval: 90s, 5m, 1h.

options.name: --above
options.description: Take a snapshot when the GC heap exceeds this size: 500MB, 2GB.

options.name: --growth
options.description: Take a snapshot when the GC heap grew by this much over the first sample: 100MB or 50%.

options.name: --rearm
options.description: After a size rule fired: once (never again), below (again after the heap falls back under it) or step (again for each further step). [default: below]

options.name: --max
options.description: Take at most this many snapshots.

options.name: --format
options.description: Output: table or csv. [default: table]

options.name: --kind
options.description: What to capture: full (a full memory dump) or gcdump (the object graph only: smaller, no field values or string text). [default: full]

commands.name: list
commands.description: List running .NET processes that can be captured.

commands.name: capture
commands.description: Capture a full memory dump (the process is paused while it is written) or, with --kind gcdump, a gcdump (the process runs one full GC). Ctrl+C cancels.

options.name: --pid
options.description: Process id to capture (see 'list').

options.name: --out
options.description: Dump file (or existing folder) to write; default: a new file in the session folder.

options.name: --session
options.description: Capture into this existing session (folder name or path under the sessions root) instead of a new one.

options.name: --label
options.description: A label for the snapshot, such as baseline.

options.name: --open
options.description: Open the snapshot after capturing it and print its summary. [default: False]

options.name: --kind
options.description: What to capture: full (a full memory dump) or gcdump (the object graph only: smaller, no field values or string text). [default: full]

commands.name: settings
commands.description: Show HeapScope's settings, or change one. They apply to the app and the command line on this machine.

options.name: --filter-text-in-logs
options.description: Write the text typed in filters and searches into HeapScope's logs (on, the default) or only its length and terms (off). The app, the worker and the command line follow it.

options.name: --dump-values-in-logs
options.description: Write the values HeapScope reads from dumps (field values and string text) into its logs (on, with --yes) or only their length (off, the default). Dumps can hold passwords, tokens and personal data. The app, the worker and the command line follow it.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Confirm turning on --dump-values-in-logs; without it, the command says what it would do and changes nothing. [default: False]

commands.name: purge
commands.description: Delete HeapScope's logs, or everything it keeps.

commands.name: logs
commands.description: Delete HeapScope's log files. Logs that running HeapScope processes write now are kept until they close.

commands.name: all
commands.description: Delete HeapScope's logs and everything in its library: sessions, captures, dumps, traces, timelines, saved indexes and bookmarks. Dumps you opened from your own folders stay.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Delete without asking; without it, Purge all only says what it would delete. [default: False]

commands.name: sample
commands.description: HeapScope's own sample process, with memory problems planted on purpose, to learn HeapScope on (the Learn page in the app).

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the sample's scenarios: what each one plants, and the type it plants.

commands.name: start
commands.description: Start the sample with the scenarios chosen and keep it running until Ctrl+C or 'sample stop'. Capture it from another terminal.

options.name: --scenarios
options.description: The scenarios to run, separated by commas (see 'sample list').

options.name: --grow
options.description: Keep growing the scenarios that can, a step every second, for Live, Compare and Trend; growth stops when the sample's heap reaches 512 MB. [default: False]

commands.name: stop
commands.description: Stop a sample that 'sample start' or the app runs. Only HeapScope's sample is stopped; any other process is refused.

options.name: --pid
options.description: The sample's process id, as 'sample start' printed it.
